The UK AI Regulation White Paper proposes to address capability gaps among regulators by prioritizing the ongoing assessment of different capability needs across the regulatory landscape. It acknowledges that regulating AI effectively will require many regulators to acquire new skills and expertise, particularly in AI technology and its interaction across multiple regulatory regimes. The government plans to work with regulators to develop guidance that helps them implement the principles in a way that aligns with expectations for how the framework should operate.

Collaborative options mentioned include:

- Engaging with organizations that provide assurance techniques and develop technical standards to identify relevant tools and embed them into the regulatory framework.
- Encouraging regulators to collaborate proactively to achieve the best outcomes for the economy and society.
- Developing joint guidance where appropriate to support industry compliance with the principles and relevant regulatory requirements.
- Sharing knowledge and cooperating across regulators to address AI use cases that interact across multiple regulatory regimes.
